name: Trinidad and Tobago
prevalence_note: Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago (CBTT Cyber Safe) & TTPS Fraud Squad 2025-2026: fake bank WhatsApp/SMS breach calls stealing OTPs, cloned-WhatsApp stranded relative/customs courier scams, and social-media vehicle/e-commerce advance-deposit fraud lead reports.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-868 within NANP; scammers mix spoofed +1-868 numbers with overseas +1 WhatsApp business accounts posing as local banks and customs agents.

scams.name: Fake Trinidad Bank Breach Alert & WhatsApp / SMS Phishing Call
scams.name_en: Impersonated local bank calling or messaging via WhatsApp/SMS to capture OTPs and logins
scams.signals_en: Caller or WhatsApp sender poses as a Trinidad commercial bank claiming an urgent account breach or failed transfer, instructing the victim to click a link or read out an MFA/OTP code.
scams.legit_en: CBTT emphasizes legitimate financial institutions never ask for personal credentials or OTPs via unsolicited text, WhatsApp, or phone calls.
bait_tactics: Say your home Wi-Fi just went offline and ask for their department so you can call the helpline on your card.
Pretend the link shows a blank page and ask them to read out the full web address letter by letter.
Ask which branch in Port of Spain or San Fernando opened your account.

scams.name: Fake Customs Courier Parcel / Relative Emergency Transfer Scam
scams.name_en: Fake courier or overseas relative claiming a high-value parcel is stuck at Customs needing fees
scams.signals_en: A supposed overseas relative or courier calls/messages on WhatsApp saying a barrel or parcel containing gifts/cash is detained at customs and needs an urgent duty transfer to a local personal bank account.
scams.legit_en: Real Trinidad customs duties are paid officially upon clearance with proper airway bills, never wired to private individuals.
bait_tactics: Say your cousin who works near Piarco will check the customs counter in person.
Call the relative's old saved number first or ask a family-specific question they cannot guess.
Pretend you need an official stamped invoice before walking into the bank.

scams.name: Social Media E-Commerce & Bargain Vehicle Advance-Deposit Scam
scams.name_en: Unverified social-media seller demanding urgent down-payment transfer before viewing
scams.signals_en: Seller advertising electronics, appliances, or a bargain vehicle insists multiple buyers are waiting and pressures an immediate bank transfer deposit before meeting in person.
scams.legit_en: CBTT Cyber Safe advises never sending money to unverified online merchants you have not met or verified.
bait_tactics: Insist on paying only after inspecting the item and certified registration papers outside a TTPS station.
Ask for the registered business street address to look up first.
Say your daily online transfer limit is set to zero and cannot be changed over the phone.
